Params: As the provisional protocol rolls out across the southern node, Karenina allows herself a small, quiet exhale.
Commandant, I'm going deeper. Someone might still be alive out there.
The operational sectors of Fenrir lie in the low ground, and the Red Tide has already flooded most of them. There is no sign of anyone left.
After turning down another corridor, Karenina halts abruptly.
Karenina's eyes move to the shut door at her side.
Mara has lost track of how long she has been sitting in Fenrir's office.
In this place, the only meaning time still holds is the finish line of a race between truth and death.
Mara's breath comes heavier now. The rot from her legs has crept up past her waist.
She has unraveled fragments of the truth: the secret embedded in the new repeaters, the nature of that special isotope, the data-devouring void at the heart of it all.
But it is not enough. One final piece still eludes her.
The blare of alarms has become background noise, as have the fights outside her door.
She no longer remembers how many days she has held on, but—
Indeed. Just hold on a little longer.
A voice sounds suddenly behind her, refined and aristocratic, haughty with privilege. An icy shudder races down Mara's spine.
You really do have some talent... To think you'd come this close.
Mara's fingers freeze above the controls. She does not dare look back.
Arius Erhorn. Though he is only a translucent projection, the faint red light bleeding from his edges makes him look like a ghost.
Ah... it's you. That explains everything.
The phantom pulses and reshapes itself, now standing right before her.
You were... that girl from the quantum repeater development team, weren't you? I rarely forget a face.
Once under my employ? Then it's no surprise you'd dig this deep... I've always recognized talent.
She looks at him with the wide-eyed terror of someone who has seen a ghost.
Surprised? That I survived? Or something else?
A mechanical limb crawls over Mara's shoulder and trails its fingertips across her cheek.
You recognize this face, don't you?
I'm rather fond of it. I like to keep it with me... It pleases me.
I'd be terribly disappointed if these eyes missed something or overlooked something...
The hand at Mara's cheek breaks apart and drifts away into the empty air.
Aren't you nearly at the answer already?
There's a little thing inside me. It loves stories. It needs information, knowledge, ideas, thoughts, all of that, so it can grow up a little faster.

After the comms went dark, the data streams flowing through the fiber-optic cables never dropped to zero. The main military channel was indeed terminated, but other signals traveling through the same cable, physically inseparable from one another, keep rushing forward alongside the transoceanic encrypted data already in transit.
And the flow only grows denser as the repair work progresses smoothly.
Mara swallows dryly, her fingers flying across the console while the data keeps streaming down the display.
Adorable... Go ahead. Play your little games.
Suppose you find your answer, what then?
The Red Tide seeps through the gap beneath the door, dark crimson liquid tasting the ground like hellish tongues.
There will be no help, of course. She knows it better than anyone. She has listened to the fighting turn to shrieks and sobbing, each cry marking one fewer comrade among the living.
Until at last, there is nothing but quiet.
I know no one's coming now. But if this answer can stop you... then I'll drag it out of the dark and leave it behind. Even if it kills me.
The Red Tide floods the room with greater speed now, surging up around Mara's ankles.
Perhaps Death will come for you. Your insides must be quite far gone by now.
The door suddenly shudders under a violent hammering.
Their eyes fly to the sound, but before a single word can leave their lips, an anchor tears through the door and sends it crashing down.
Mara looks up into a pair of eyes burning like fire, framed by a white captain's coat already smudged with ash and smoke.
Karenina barrels through the doorway and scans the room, her gaze skipping across the consoles and glowing screens before it finally finds Mara.
She has held on alone, pursuing the truth to the bitter end, yet she never expected anyone to come for her in such hopelessness.
That distant silhouette she could never reach has opened the door and returned to her side, in a different form.
The girl should not be here. She must not be seen by the devil.
At once, the small space swarms with ghostly red images that press in around Karenina until she is entirely encircled.
As if the curtain has risen on a long-awaited performance, he claps with great relish and amusement.
She glares at the man before her, her knuckles whitening around the weapon's grip.
Since you first arrived on these waters... you've changed, in a rather pleasing way.
But I don't like your eyes. Nor the way you look at me.
Karenina wrenches her anchor forward and smashes it into the phantom. The red projection dissipates like smoke, then rematerializes behind her an instant later.
Arius lifts his hands in a subtle, graceful motion, and the nameless crimson phantoms coil around Karenina.
Her M.I.N.D. roils, surging in wild, unsteady waves.
You... remind me of certain people, disobedient ones.
That was an encounter worth holding onto.
Kalon's face fit every cliche of the career scientist, yet his eyes burned with a quiet, stubborn fire.
All the experimental data has been destroyed, you said?
I destroyed everything related to the "cerebrospinal fluid" immediately. Mara will handle the quantum decoherence spectral data...
Of course not! The Ytterbium-174 copolymer is the Science Council's highest classified secret. I signed the NDA—

...Speaking of which. I believe we need to completely eliminate the Ytterbium-174X3 doping from all future entanglement crystal production. This vulnerability is catastrophic. If anyone were to exploit it, the entire fiber-optic network would become—
Yes, yes. I know. You're always so scrupulous... Now, the point. You know what I care about.
Kalon's expression lit up with a hint of excitement.
...The Ytterbium-174 isotope may represent a new direction. It could stabilize the test subjects and restore a normal growth cycle. Its properties are extraordinary.
All preliminary data support it. If we pursue this—
An odd look settled across Arius' features, something that could have been delight.
Or revulsion. Kalon could not be sure.
My brilliant scientist, set aside quantum communications... Let's turn our minds to something truly meaningful.
From now on, you have my full support. Every resource. Every possibility. The ones you dream of, and the ones you haven't dreamed yet.
And climb toward the pinnacle of truth. Though, of course...
He noticed the crease in Kalon's brow and allowed himself a small, knowing smile.
It's for Cordy as well. This will help her... won't it?
Of course. My door is always open.
Mr. Erhorn, about the crystal doping for the quantum repeater... the matter Dr. Kalon raised...
It's captured your imagination, hasn't it? The entire world's information lifeline, held in one's hand. Even the smallest crack in that door is rather... intoxicating.
...Succumbing to temptation is perfectly human. I don't blame you for it.
By all means. Do whatever you wish.
Our dear, principled Dr. Kalon won't have the luxury of worrying about your quantum repeater any longer.
Truth, after all, stretches as boundlessly as the sea, yet a single person can only catch the murmur of its waves.
And that murmur alone is enough to resound through a lifetime.
Driven by the tides, the Red Tide now heaves in waves that match the ocean's own immensity.
Pushing past the pain, Karenina launches yet another crushing attack at Arius.
But this time, the crimson phantom intercepts the hit, absorbing it completely.
What a generous reunion present my brilliant scientist prepared for me.
I confess, I thought you were dead. All those useless failures before you broke so quickly.
Even you, a theoretical success, preserved this long... it's practically a miracle.
"Preserved." A flicker runs through Karenina's gaze at the word.
Arius pushes the anchor away and tosses it aside, letting it crash into the control console nearby.
I read through your Construct modification dossier. Do you know what I found?
The corner of Arius' eye gives an almost invisible flicker.
"A spike that should never have existed."
You were the success that should never have happened. And yet, here you are.
What the Erhorn family has yearned for across centuries, our dream made flesh.
The Construct girl takes a steadying breath and summons her anchor back.
The moment the anchor touched the console, it began a full-spectrum search for the communication node Arius exploited to infiltrate. The weapon has already locked on.
...Oh? Splitting your focus mid-fight is not the best habit to have.
The girl delivers a massive, sweeping blow through the countless red phantoms, and in that instant, the figures that had been solid enough to strike back dissolve into empty shadows again.
The girl carefully lifts Mara up, her gaze fixed with worry on the ruined, festering skin.
The decaying phantoms still hold the faintest outline of a human shape.
The crimson haze spreads and wracks Mara with harsh, hacking coughs.
Has it never crossed your mind? Why Kalon took you in?
A mad scientist who committed unspeakable atrocities under my patronage. What would drive someone like that to adopt a stray orphan?
Unless he recognized you... There's really no other plausible explanation.
A child born from his crowning achievement. In a way... a very fine trophy to keep.
Mara fights her way upright, her voice shaking with anger.
He was not a mad scientist... Dr. Kalon was...
Karenina lifts her chin, and her eyes burn with scorching fury as she fixes them on Arius.
No matter. As a tool, you've finally been set to your proper purpose... Restoring the glory of the Erhorn family, and of humanity, should be honor enough for you.
Through the flickering, distorted projection, Karenina's mind drifts to her grandfather's weathered eyes and the gentle embrace she felt in that dream.
You've never had anyone who really loves you, right?
Only a moron would fall for your garbage.
That villain monologue? Seriously? God, you're so lame.
I know what being loved feels like. I know Grandpa's heart was real. I know what it means to be protected, cared about, and believed in.
Every bit of kindness and love I've ever known was real. So...
Don't think for a second your poison can rewrite the person who loved me.
I don't need you to tell me who my grandpa was.
A flicker of something ugly crosses Arius' features in the shadows, there and gone.
I do admire your composure. Hold onto it, my...
Before the echo of his voice can die away, Karenina's heavy strike obliterates the final trace of his murmuring.
As the last trace of the figure fades, Arius snaps his fingers.
The familiar whale calls echo again.
Karenina readies herself for the pain, but what arrives with it is a tide of broken pieces from deep inside her M.I.N.D.
Memories fall like unsorted letters from long ago, drifting like snowflakes, spinning a small blizzard through her M.I.N.D.
At the storm's heart, a child reaches desperately forward and catches only the frayed edge of a bond long cut.
She remembers a whale launching itself from the sea, the blast that roared beside her ear.
She remembers the cold, indifferent eyes that watched her in the laboratory. The young woman who hid her from the hunt, and how her gaze went dark before the end.
She remembers ash clouds rising like gray cotton candy, a cargo ship dissolving in fire like melting ice cream, and missiles carving through an upside-down sky.
The young woman who held her said they were pretty balloons. So many of them.
It was the first fairy tale she ever heard.
So many balloons... Look how high they're flying... so high...
They're flying all the way to the heart of the sea...

The rippled blue glass was a sea on fire. The mushroom cloud climbing skyward was nothing like cotton candy. The missiles that filled the sky like balloons screamed as they flew up, and the heat that melted everything burned her eyes.
The world met her with its ugliest face, but the young woman who held her taught her this:
Love will give you the eyes to truly see the world.
Love will give you the eyes to truly see the world.
Red... is the color of flowers... and kisses...
Her shredded memories stitch themselves together in chaotic fragments. Karenina lifts her hand and finds a single drop of moisture at the corner of her eye.
She cannot tell if the tear belongs to this present ache or if she is finally paying back a debt of tears from years ago.
The world is still wailing, as it did on that day, as it does today. But the baby, once a "little monster," now knows how to feel both happiness and sorrow.
The pain brought by the whale calls makes her hands tremble. Grief and joy twist together, and the tears fall like instinct, splashing one drop by one onto the back of her hand.
The old woman clasps her shaking hand, and Karenina grips back, her fingers curling tightly around Mara's thin, frail ones.
(She's flying to the heart of the sea, too...)
You didn't have to come for me... silly girl.
She gives a small cough, and blood threads from the corner of her mouth.
I should've... I should've been faster.
Karenina... the new repeaters... there's a "trap" planted in them.
No. Listen. Just listen... The Global Optimization Protocol we brought... it's been compromised...
After the protocol update... the control center that set the trap will gain priority over all traffic.
Every piece of data... when it enters the three nodes... a copy is made, sent to a hidden buffer pool.
There's... something in there. A black hole that never fills. I don't know... what kind of thing could swallow that much data...
She heaves, and a thick gush of dark red blood pours from her lips.
...Mara! Stop talking! I'm getting you out of here.
The girl hoists the old woman who can no longer stand alone and pushes forward, slow step by slow step...
On the girl's cheek, the tears she could not cry as a baby finally fall, and a pair of thin, weathered hands brushes them gently away.
The dying woman opens her mouth as if there are still words left inside her.
I told you... I was there during your surgery. When you were still human, your brain structure was different. Wise and I hid it together.
Your body adapted well to Tantalum-193... but more precisely... to another element inside it. Ytterbium-174...
Wise and I... we wanted to keep you far from all of this.
You were dying. Even without what happened... your body... it couldn't carry you anymore. The Construct modification was the only choice left.
I... I couldn't watch you die. Not you. You were everything he left behind... the only... you were all I had left of him.
I know. I don't blame you... I could never blame you...
Don't listen to that devil... Your heart never lied to you. You are loved.
Kalon loved you. And I... I also...
The word still will not come.
She has chased that silhouette for too long, as if it were a gleam of light, a distant ideal, a feeling too delicate to hold up to the light.
She has chased it so long that she cannot even say what it means anymore.
And yet, for a moment, she truly seems to see that moon.
The moon... so far away... I gave everything... and I still can't catch up...
Don't say that... We're almost there...
Don't be sad, Karenina... The path to death... isn't always terrifying...
Her pupils widen by slow degrees, and her eyes grow empty, gazing at something far beyond.
The ocean wind takes away her last sigh.
When Karenina walks out of Fenrir, sunset spreads across the water, and even the Red Tide-tainted sea catches the light in shimmers of gold.
Her gaze falls on a carving in the platform's wall, worn down by years of salt and wind, a last testament from someone forgotten.
Karenina presses her palm against the wall and lowers her head into the crook of her arm. At last, she allows herself to cry out loud.
For a sacrifice so small and "foolish."
